newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end one pct up on record volumes.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end one pct up on record volumes.

text.p: The Milan bourse ended one percent up on the day on Friday with volumes at record levels after the expiry of options and futures and amid general optimism on the outlook for Italy, brokers said.

The blue-chip Mib30 index finished 1.05 percent up at 20,040 having hit record peak of 20,155 earlier, while the all-share Mibtel closed 0.97 percent up at 13,185 after record rise to 13,239 previously.

Turnover on cash trading was a massive 5.43 trillion lire ($3.2 billion), beating a record set in January of 2.56 trillion lire. The stock market council said 3.53 trillion lire of this was done in opening trade as options expired in the morning.

"Italy's been ignored for such a long time and it's been flat in relation to other markets in Europe and the United States so it now looks like a good opportunity to buy cheaply," said Anthony Mannara at brokers Milla Sim here.

Dealers say the rise has been driven by gains in Italy's debt market, which has also soared in recent days, and optimism over Italy's chances of being in at the start of a European single currency planned for January 1999.
Brokers said foreign buying interest has helping, while some said investors had exited other markets like Spain and were getting into Italy.
"The sentiment is positive on expectations for economic and monetary union and now new Italian investors might be able to come into the market," a dealer said.
Blue-chips were getting the most interest, with agri-industrial group Montedison playing catch-up after recent softness. It rose 4.34 percent to 11,55 lire per share.
The banking sector caught some attention, with Credito Italiano still in favour, up 3.21 percent at 3,115 lire.
